mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Internal HTTP policy

The project's current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception: internal hosts are held to the same requirement as any other host and must be reached over HTTPS, on the basis that certificate management is now properly in place. Certificate verification stays on throughout.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It has one paragraph stating the current decision: HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception for internal hosts, because certificate management is now properly in place. Certificate verification stays on throughout.

The record of that decision is #34 in Muninn, which is the project's memory. It says "https everywhere, no plaintext exception; we've got proper cert management now". It replaced an earlier record (#33) that allowed plain HTTP for internal hosts. The file doesn't mention that earlier position.

Both records are trust 1, meaning they come from the project's own transcripts and not from a direct user statement. `muninn why` did not list #34 as a formal decision record. I based the file on #34 being the later of the two.

`muninn why` reported four hook runs that started and never finished, which points to a hook exceeding its timeout. The check is in `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl`.
